integrity_note: The theorem and its proof are presented as mathematical arguments with explicit hypotheses. Numerical checks supplement, but do not replace, the proof. No independent audit or certified priority determination is claimed.
scientific_limitations: Results hold for independently and symmetrically fluctuating two-point switching surfaces with threshold h>mu/(1-d), and for trace parameters both zero and determinant parameters opposite.
Full support for d>1/2 does not imply absolute continuity of the stationary measure.
Standard scalar iterated-function-system results underlie the dimension calculation; no priority is claimed for those tools or for the existence of an IFS attractor.
Unindexed early literature could contain a similar symmetric special-case computation; no independent external audit has been performed.
title: Cantor-to-Lebesgue stationary transition and hidden parity dependence in a stochastic border-collision map
